page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, accompanied by 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache. Memory is provisioned at 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes hardware instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES, which assist vector math and cryptographic operations. It includes zero bundled local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier multi-threaded compute and throughput. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 15418.2 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7164.0, while Geekbench software compilation reaches 12321.0. Read-only large-block memory bandwidth settles at 82.43 GB/sec with write bandwidth at 42.68 GB/sec. Workload-specific tests show strong transactional throughput, processing 14.12 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining 12.3 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. However, single-core processing shows limitations: stress-ng single-core performance and bzip3 decompression metrics both score within the lower 25 percent tier.

The 1.0 GB of memory per vCPU provides a lean configuration where raw core count takes precedence over memory footprint. Because bundled local storage is absent, external network disks must be attached, introducing an I/O dependency for disk-heavy tasks. Cost efficiency is driven by high parallel processing capacity per core allocation rather than raw single-threaded performance or memory density. The instance is suited for parallelized compilation, lightweight web serving, batch processing, and CPU-bound microservices that do not demand extensive working memory.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-16 is a compute-skewed virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.8 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it supports AVX-512 vector and VNNI instructions. The instance contains no bundled local storage and no GPU hardware, requiring persistent network disks for persistent storage. Benchmark data indicates solid mid-range multi-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 7164.0, a PassMark CPU score of 15418.2, and 14.12 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-thread stress tests and bzip3 decompression register in the lower performance quartile. The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio creates an efficient environment for parallel execution that minimizes memory footprint, making it appropriate for distributed compilation, static web serving fleets, batch transcoding, and microservice workloads.
